description: Seed registry of hypotheses, conventions and presets for closed-loop null-space exploration (epic #12593). Seeded by NSX-00 (#12549). Loader and CI citation gate land in NSX-11 (#12556).

schema_note.hypotheses: id, statement, parameters, source, verification_status. A hypothesis is a physiological or modelling prior that conditions a FAMILY_DEPENDENT output. statement is user-facing and must not rely on a source whose verification_status is UNVERIFIED or REMOVED.
schema_note.conventions: id, statement, parameters. A convention is a choice of metric, scale or frame; it is not physiology and never appears in an INVARIANT claim as a hypothesis.
schema_note.presets: id, label, hypotheses, conventions. A preset is a named hypothesis set for the UI; every id must exist.
schema_note.torque_capacity: NSX-04 (#12553). One entry per coordinate (joint_slot, the spec coordinate name) and direction (negative or positive generalised-coordinate sign; root translations are excluded because they are forces). Fields: joint_slot, direction, motion, tau_max_nm (value for the reference subject 78 kg / 1.71 m, or the unscaled population value), scaling_rule {rule: none | bw_height_normalized, coefficient, reference_subject, formula}, population, source {citation_id, location, note}, verification_status, assumed (bool), axis_mapping (hinge | approximate-at-reference-pose) and axis_evidence (file:line or frame derivation), optional force_velocity, basis, rationale. VERIFIED means the number was read in the cited source and the sign-to-motion mapping is unambiguous from the spec; anything else sets assumed=true, verification_status=UNVERIFIED and a rationale. Capacities are male population priors, not subject measurements.
schema_note.source: Object {citation_id | null, note}. citation_id refers to citations[] below.
schema_note.verification_status: One of VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, REMOVED, NOT_APPLICABLE (a modelling choice with no empirical claim).

hypotheses.statement: Each actuated joint can sustain a torque of at most its declared capacity in each direction; torques beyond capacity are excluded from the feasible set.

source.note: Capacities are a population prior; values and sources arrive with NSX-04.

hypotheses.statement: Among admissible allocations, the representative minimises the sum of squared torques each divided by its joint capacity.

source.note: Modelling choice; requires H-TORQUE-CAPACITY.

hypotheses.statement: The representative penalises the squared torque rate, favouring smooth torque histories.

source.note: Modelling choice.

hypotheses.statement: Positive and negative joint power carry separate costs c_plus and c_minus; with c_plus equal to c_minus the cost reduces to a net-power term plus absolute power.

source.note: Modelling choice; identity proved in the specification.

hypotheses.statement: Each hand keeps at least a declared axial squeeze on the club, so hand contact never goes slack.

source.note: Preload magnitudes are not sourced here; Choi and Park 2020 measured internal grip forces but no value is adopted.

hypotheses.statement: Contact loads lie inside a friction cone with a declared coefficient, approximated by a polyhedron with a declared facet count and error bound.

source.note: Modelling choice.

conventions.statement: Closure rows and hand wrenches are expressed in the grip frame: origin at the midpoint of the two grip points, u along the shaft toward the clubhead, v the face-normal projection orthogonal to u, w = u x v.

parameters.sign: +J_c^T lambda acts on the tree; the closing hand exerts -lambda on the club

conventions.statement: Torque norms are weighted by inverse squared joint capacity.
Torque norms use the identity metric on actuated torques.
Torque norms use the inverse mass matrix on actuated coordinates; this is a labelled metric and is not Gauss's principle.
Forces are scaled by a characteristic force and moments by a characteristic moment before rank decisions and in null-space coordinates.
Numerical rank uses a relative singular-value tolerance against the largest singular value of the scaled matrix.

torque_capacity.motion: shoulder horizontal abduction/adduction (rotation about the vertical axis at zero pose)

source.note: Saul 2015 Table 2 abduction/adduction is a different axis; not adopted as a value for this axis.

torque_capacity.rationale: Axes resolved from the spec: the zero pose has the arm along +X (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:41); the shoulder child frame has x_c = parent +Z, y_c = parent +Y, z_c = parent -X (joints[] 'Shoulder Joint' parent_to_base), so X is a vertical-axis swing, Y flexion/extension, Z axial rotation. No readable source gives isometric shoulder torque about these axes: Saul 2015 (read) reports only frontal-plane abduction 58.1 and adduction 75.7 Nm about the anterior-posterior axis, which is none of the three gimbal axes; Hughes 1999 (flexion, extension, rotation) is paywalled and unread. 58.1 Nm is the abduction value used as an order-of-magnitude placeholder.
torque_capacity.axis_evidence: Frames at zero pose are aligned with the trunk (parent_to_base rotation is identity); the model faces +X with +Z up (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:41, ARM_FORWARD), so rotation about +X is lateral bend, about +Y (left-right) is flexion/extension with positive = forward tilt, about +Z is axial rotation. Spec: full_body_spec_anthro_driver.json joints[] parent_to_base.

source.note: Saul 2015 Table 2 abduction/adduction is a different axis; not adopted as a value for this axis.

torque_capacity.rationale: Axes resolved from the spec: the zero pose has the arm along +X (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:41); the shoulder child frame has x_c = parent +Z, y_c = parent +Y, z_c = parent -X (joints[] 'Shoulder Joint' parent_to_base), so X is a vertical-axis swing, Y flexion/extension, Z axial rotation.
